question.text: In what weather do most crashes happen?

answer.text: Most crashes happen in clear weather rather than in snow, rain or fog, so a pleasant day can be just as deadly.

teaching.text: Asked "In what weather do most crashes happen?" a tempting wrong answer is "Snow", but most happen in clear weather. Remember: Clear days are deadly too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Most crashes happen in clear weather rather than in snow, rain or fog, so a pleasant day can be just as deadly.

question.text: What do many drivers do when a collision seems about to happen?

answer.text: When a collision seems about to happen, many drivers panic and do nothing, yet there is almost always some action that can avoid the crash or lessen it.

teaching.text: Asked "A collision seems about to happen. What does the manual say is almost always possible?" a tempting wrong answer is "Nothing can be done", but some action almost always helps. Remember: Never just freeze.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a collision seems about to happen, many drivers panic and do nothing, yet there is almost always some action that can avoid the crash or lessen it.

question.text: What are the three ways to avoid a collision?

answer.text: To avoid a collision a driver has three options: stop, turn, or speed up.

teaching.text: The stop, turn or speed up rule names stopping, turning and speeding up as the options, and the when to speed up rule says when speeding up is the right one. Remember: Stop, turn or speed up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To avoid a collision a driver has three options: stop, turn, or speed up.

question.text: Why read your owner's manual about brakes?

answer.text: Read your vehicle owner's manual to learn how its antilock braking system works, since antilock brakes let you stop without skidding.

teaching.text: Asked "Why should you read your owner's manual about the braking system?" a tempting wrong answer is "To learn the radio presets", but to learn the antilock system. Remember: Know your antilock system.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Read your vehicle owner's manual to learn how its antilock braking system works, since antilock brakes let you stop without skidding.

question.text: How do you stop quickly with antilock brakes?

answer.text: To stop quickly with antilock brakes, press the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep firm pressure on it, without letting up even when the pedal pushes back.

teaching.text: The hard stop with antilock brakes rule has you press as hard as you can with antilock brakes, while the hard stop without antilock brakes rule has you brake hard without locking the wheels when you have none. Remember: Press hard and hold.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To stop quickly with antilock brakes, press the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep firm pressure on it, without letting up even when the pedal pushes back.

question.text: How do you stop quickly without antilock brakes?

answer.text: To stop quickly without antilock brakes, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels, since braking too hard or too long can cause a skid.

teaching.text: The hard stop with antilock brakes rule has you press as hard as you can with antilock brakes, while the hard stop without antilock brakes rule has you brake hard without locking the wheels when you have none. Remember: Hard, but no lockup.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To stop quickly without antilock brakes, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels, since braking too hard or too long can cause a skid.

question.text: Without antilock brakes, what do you do if the wheels lock?

answer.text: Without antilock brakes, if the wheels lock and you feel a skid, let up on the pedal quickly, then press down again once the skid stops, repeating until the car stops.

teaching.text: The releasing a locked skid rule has you let up and press again after a lockup without antilock brakes, while the never pump antilock brakes rule says never to pump antilock brakes. Remember: Let up, press again.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Without antilock brakes, if the wheels lock and you feel a skid, let up on the pedal quickly, then press down again once the skid stops, repeating until the car stops.

question.text: How do antilock brakes change an emergency stop?

answer.text: In an emergency with antilock brakes the wheels do not lock and the car can still be steered, while without them all wheels may lock and the skidding car cannot be steered properly.

teaching.text: Asked "In an emergency stop, what can you still do with antilock brakes that you cannot with locked wheels?" a tempting wrong answer is "Stop in zero feet", but you can still steer. Remember: Antilock lets you steer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In an emergency with antilock brakes the wheels do not lock and the car can still be steered, while without them all wheels may lock and the skidding car cannot be steered properly.

question.text: Should you pump antilock brakes when the pedal pulses?

answer.text: Never pump the brake pedal in a car with antilock brakes, even when the pedal pulses; the pulsing is the system pumping the brakes faster than you could.

teaching.text: The releasing a locked skid rule has you let up and press again after a lockup without antilock brakes, while the never pump antilock brakes rule says never to pump antilock brakes. Remember: Never pump antilock.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never pump the brake pedal in a car with antilock brakes, even when the pedal pulses; the pulsing is the system pumping the brakes faster than you could.

question.text: What should your foot do when antilock brakes pulse and rattle?

answer.text: With antilock brakes, keep your foot firmly on the pedal despite the pulsing and noise, because easing off ruins the system's advantage.

teaching.text: The never pump antilock brakes rule says never to pump antilock brakes, and the keep the foot firm rule says to keep your foot firm despite the pulsing. Remember: Stay firm through pulsing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With antilock brakes, keep your foot firmly on the pedal despite the pulsing and noise, because easing off ruins the system's advantage.

question.text: Should antilock brakes make you drive more aggressively?

answer.text: Never drive a car with antilock brakes more aggressively than one without them.

teaching.text: Asked "How should you drive a car with antilock brakes compared with one without?" a tempting wrong answer is "Much faster", but no more aggressively. Remember: Same caution either way.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never drive a car with antilock brakes more aggressively than one without them.

question.text: If you cannot stop in time, what should you do?

answer.text: In most cases you can turn your vehicle faster than you can stop it, so if you cannot stop in time, steer around the hazard and brake only if you must.

teaching.text: The turning beats stopping rule says you can usually turn faster than you can stop, and the off the road over head-on rule says driving off the road beats a head-on crash. Remember: Steer around it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In most cases you can turn your vehicle faster than you can stop it, so if you cannot stop in time, steer around the hazard and brake only if you must.

question.text: Where should your hands be for quick turns?

answer.text: For quick turns, grip the wheel with both hands on opposite sides at about the nine o'clock and three o'clock positions, which also keeps your wrists and forearms out of the air bag's main impact area.

teaching.text: The nine and three grip rule sets the nine and three grip, while the quick left turn hands rule describes how the hands move in a quick left turn. Remember: Nine and three.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For quick turns, grip the wheel with both hands on opposite sides at about the nine o'clock and three o'clock positions, which also keeps your wrists and forearms out of the air bag's main impact area.

question.text: How do your hands move in a quick left turn?

answer.text: For a quick evasive turn to the left, the right hand swings from three o'clock toward nine o'clock as far as needed while the left hand slides toward the bottom of the wheel to steady the grip.

teaching.text: The nine and three grip rule sets the nine and three grip, while the quick left turn hands rule describes how the hands move in a quick left turn. Remember: Right hand swings over.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a quick evasive turn to the left, the right hand swings from three o'clock toward nine o'clock as far as needed while the left hand slides toward the bottom of the wheel to steady the grip.

question.text: How do you regain your lane after clearing a hazard?

answer.text: As you clear the hazard, turn the wheel back to the right to regain your lane, then left just enough to straighten out, returning your hands to nine and three; for a quick right turn, mirror every step.

teaching.text: Asked "After clearing a hazard with a quick left turn, how do you regain your lane?" a tempting wrong answer is "Keep turning left", but turn back right, then straighten. Remember: Back, straighten, nine three.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: As you clear the hazard, turn the wheel back to the right to regain your lane, then left just enough to straighten out, returning your hands to nine and three; for a quick right turn, mirror every step.

question.text: What must you be ready for after steering away from a hazard?

answer.text: After steering away from a hazard, be ready to keep control and steer where you want the car to go, because some drivers dodge one crash only to cause another.

teaching.text: Asked "After steering away from a hazard, what must you be ready to do?" a tempting wrong answer is "Let go of the wheel", but keep control. Remember: Keep control after.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After steering away from a hazard, be ready to keep control and steer where you want the car to go, because some drivers dodge one crash only to cause another.

question.text: Can you steer while braking with antilock brakes?

answer.text: With antilock brakes you can steer while braking without skidding, which helps when you must swerve and stop or slow quickly.

teaching.text: Asked "Why do antilock brakes help when you must swerve and stop quickly?" a tempting wrong answer is "They turn the car for you", but they let you steer while braking. Remember: Brake and steer together.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With antilock brakes you can steer while braking without skidding, which helps when you must swerve and stop or slow quickly.

question.text: Without antilock brakes, how do you turn quickly?

answer.text: Without antilock brakes, to turn quickly you must let up on the brake pedal and then turn the wheel.

teaching.text: The let up, then turn rule says to let up on the brake before turning without antilock brakes, while the brake before turning rule says braking first shifts weight forward to help the turn. Remember: Release, then turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Without antilock brakes, to turn quickly you must let up on the brake pedal and then turn the wheel.

question.text: Why brake before a quick turn without antilock brakes?

answer.text: Braking before a quick turn without antilock brakes slows the car and shifts weight onto the front tires, which lets it turn faster.

teaching.text: The let up, then turn rule says to let up on the brake before turning without antilock brakes, while the brake before turning rule says braking first shifts weight forward to help the turn. Remember: Weight forward helps turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Braking before a quick turn without antilock brakes slows the car and shifts weight onto the front tires, which lets it turn faster.

question.text: What should you do if the front wheels lock?

answer.text: Stop braking if you feel the front wheels lock, and do not turn so sharply that the car can only plow straight ahead.

teaching.text: Asked "You feel the front wheels lock while braking and turning. What should you do?" a tempting wrong answer is "Brake harder", but stop braking. Remember: Stop braking on lockup.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stop braking if you feel the front wheels lock, and do not turn so sharply that the car can only plow straight ahead.

question.text: Is it better to drive off the road or crash head-on?

answer.text: It is generally better to drive off the road than to crash head-on into another vehicle.

teaching.text: The turning beats stopping rule says you can usually turn faster than you can stop, and the off the road over head-on rule says driving off the road beats a head-on crash. Remember: Off road beats head-on.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: It is generally better to drive off the road than to crash head-on into another vehicle.

question.text: When can speeding up be the right move?

answer.text: Speeding up can be the right move when another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or behind and there is room ahead, but slow down once the danger passes.

teaching.text: The stop, turn or speed up rule names stopping, turning and speeding up as the options, and the when to speed up rule says when speeding up is the right one. Remember: Speed up to escape.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Speeding up can be the right move when another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or behind and there is room ahead, but slow down once the danger passes.

question.text: Why should you not jerk the wheel in an emergency?

answer.text: Do not freeze at the wheel or jerk it suddenly in an emergency, because a jerk can send you into another object or off the road and into a rollover.

teaching.text: The never lock the ignition moving rule warns that locking the ignition while moving locks the steering, while the do not freeze or jerk rule warns against jerking the wheel. Remember: No freezing, no jerking.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not freeze at the wheel or jerk it suddenly in an emergency, because a jerk can send you into another object or off the road and into a rollover.

question.text: How should you use antilock braking to avoid an obstacle?

answer.text: Use the antilock system's nonskid ability to steer around the obstacle that made you brake, and keep steering to a safe place once past it.

teaching.text: Asked "With antilock brakes, how can you get past the obstacle that made you brake?" a tempting wrong answer is "Hold straight and hope", but steer around it. Remember: Brake and steer away.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use the antilock system's nonskid ability to steer around the obstacle that made you brake, and keep steering to a safe place once past it.

question.text: How can you practice antilock braking?

answer.text: To practice antilock braking, use a big empty lot without curbs or many light poles, drive about twenty miles per hour, slam the brakes and steer, later steering around a cardboard box as a target.

teaching.text: Asked "Where does the manual suggest practicing antilock braking?" a tempting wrong answer is "A busy street", but a big empty lot. Remember: Empty lot practice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To practice antilock braking, use a big empty lot without curbs or many light poles, drive about twenty miles per hour, slam the brakes and steer, later steering around a cardboard box as a target.

question.text: What season is peak for deer crashes?

answer.text: Fall is the peak season for deer crashes, because autumn's mating and hunting seasons make deer more active and likely to wander.

teaching.text: Asked "Which season is the peak season for deer crashes?" a tempting wrong answer is "Spring", but fall. Remember: Fall brings deer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fall is the peak season for deer crashes, because autumn's mating and hunting seasons make deer more active and likely to wander.

question.text: Which animal crashes are the most dangerous and costly?

answer.text: Crashes with deer are generally the most dangerous and costly kind of animal crash.

teaching.text: Asked "Which kind of animal crash is generally the most dangerous and costly?" a tempting wrong answer is "A crash with a rabbit", but deer crashes. Remember: Deer crashes cost most.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crashes with deer are generally the most dangerous and costly kind of animal crash.

question.text: When and where should you watch most for deer?

answer.text: Be especially alert for deer at dusk and dawn, when they come out to feed, and near woods and water.

teaching.text: Asked "When should you be especially alert for deer?" a tempting wrong answer is "At noon", but at dusk and dawn. Remember: Dusk, dawn, woods, water.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Be especially alert for deer at dusk and dawn, when they come out to feed, and near woods and water.

question.text: You see one deer. What should you expect?

answer.text: If you see one deer, expect that several others may be close by.

teaching.text: Asked "A deer crosses the road ahead of you. What should you expect?" a tempting wrong answer is "It is always alone", but others may be close by. Remember: Expect more deer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you see one deer, expect that several others may be close by.

question.text: When can animal crashes happen?

answer.text: Animal crashes can happen in any season and with any animal, from opossums and rabbits to dogs, and while many deer crashes occur at night, they can happen at any hour.

teaching.text: Asked "When can animal crashes happen?" a tempting wrong answer is "Only in fall", but in any season. Remember: Any season, any hour.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Animal crashes can happen in any season and with any animal, from opossums and rabbits to dogs, and while many deer crashes occur at night, they can happen at any hour.

question.text: Is there a foolproof way to keep deer off highways?

answer.text: No foolproof method has been found to keep deer and other wild animals off highways.

teaching.text: Asked "Is there a foolproof method to keep deer off highways?" a tempting wrong answer is "Yes, whistles", but no foolproof method exists. Remember: Nothing is foolproof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No foolproof method has been found to keep deer and other wild animals off highways.

question.text: How can you avoid deer?

answer.text: To avoid deer, heed deer crossing signs, look far down the road and well off to each side, and at night use high beams when you can to light the road edges.

teaching.text: The watching for deer rule says to use high beams to light the road edges, while the deer fixate on lights rule warns that flashing your lights at a deer may freeze it. Remember: Signs, scanning, high beams.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To avoid deer, heed deer crossing signs, look far down the road and well off to each side, and at night use high beams when you can to light the road edges.

question.text: What should you scan the roadsides for at night?

answer.text: Scan the roadsides for your headlights reflecting in a deer's eyes.

teaching.text: Asked "What should you scan the roadsides for at night to spot deer?" a tempting wrong answer is "Road signs only", but reflections in a deer's eyes. Remember: Shining eyes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Scan the roadsides for your headlights reflecting in a deer's eyes.

question.text: What should you do if you have time to avoid an animal?

answer.text: If you have time to avoid an animal ahead, slow down, tap your brakes to warn drivers behind you, and sound your horn.

teaching.text: The slow, tap and honk rule has you slow, tap the brakes and honk when there is time, while the do not swerve for animals rule says not to swerve when hitting the animal seems unavoidable. Remember: Slow, tap, honk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you have time to avoid an animal ahead, slow down, tap your brakes to warn drivers behind you, and sound your horn.

question.text: Why not flash your lights at a deer?

answer.text: Deer tend to fixate on headlights, so flashing your lights at one may make it freeze in the road.

teaching.text: The watching for deer rule says to use high beams to light the road edges, while the deer fixate on lights rule warns that flashing your lights at a deer may freeze it. Remember: Flashing freezes deer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Deer tend to fixate on headlights, so flashing your lights at one may make it freeze in the road.

question.text: How hard should you brake for an animal with no one close behind?

answer.text: If no vehicle is close behind you, brake hard for an animal but do not lock the wheels into a skid.

teaching.text: Asked "No vehicle is close behind you and an animal is ahead. How should you brake?" a tempting wrong answer is "Gently only", but brake hard without locking. Remember: Hard, no skid.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If no vehicle is close behind you, brake hard for an animal but do not lock the wheels into a skid.

question.text: Should you swerve if hitting an animal seems unavoidable?

answer.text: If hitting an animal seems unavoidable, do not swerve, since swerving may raise your risk of injury; keep the car under control and on the road.

teaching.text: The slow, tap and honk rule has you slow, tap the brakes and honk when there is time, while the do not swerve for animals rule says not to swerve when hitting the animal seems unavoidable. Remember: Do not swerve.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If hitting an animal seems unavoidable, do not swerve, since swerving may raise your risk of injury; keep the car under control and on the road.

question.text: Whom do you tell after hitting a deer or farm animal?

answer.text: Report a crash with a large animal such as a deer or farm animal to the police.

teaching.text: Asked "Whom should you report a crash with a farm animal to?" a tempting wrong answer is "No one", but report it to the police. Remember: Report it to police.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Report a crash with a large animal such as a deer or farm animal to the police.

question.text: What should you do after hitting a pet near homes?

answer.text: If you hit a domestic pet near homes, try to let the owner know if you can.

teaching.text: Asked "You hit a domestic pet on a residential street. What should you try to do?" a tempting wrong answer is "Drive away", but let the owner know. Remember: Tell the owner.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you hit a domestic pet near homes, try to let the owner know if you can.

question.text: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

answer.text: Human error is the single most common cause of traffic crashes, and the leading factors are excessive speed, lack of concentration and improper evasive action.

teaching.text: The human error rule names human error as the most common cause of crashes, while the driver, vehicle and road rule names the driver, vehicle and road as the three parts of the system. Remember: Human error leads.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Human error is the single most common cause of traffic crashes, and the leading factors are excessive speed, lack of concentration and improper evasive action.

question.text: What are the three parts of the highway system?

answer.text: Safe driving depends on three parts of the highway system, the driver, the vehicle and the road, and neglecting any of them contributes to most crashes.

teaching.text: The human error rule names human error as the most common cause of crashes, while the driver, vehicle and road rule names the driver, vehicle and road as the three parts of the system. Remember: Driver, vehicle, road.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Safe driving depends on three parts of the highway system, the driver, the vehicle and the road, and neglecting any of them contributes to most crashes.

question.text: How does a good driver differ from a careless one?

answer.text: A good driver takes pride in caring for the vehicle, obeys traffic laws and respects others, while a careless driver neglects all three.

teaching.text: Asked "Which describes a good driver?" a tempting wrong answer is "Drives fastest", but cares, obeys and respects. Remember: Care, obey, respect.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A good driver takes pride in caring for the vehicle, obeys traffic laws and respects others, while a careless driver neglects all three.

question.text: How many yearly crashes does the manual tie to poor habits?

answer.text: The manual attributes about one hundred sixty thousand crashes reported to the Department of Safety each year to poor driving habits.

teaching.text: Asked "About how many yearly crashes reported to the Department of Safety does the manual attribute to poor driving habits?" a tempting wrong answer is "About one hundred", but about one hundred sixty thousand. Remember: Poor habits cause crashes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual attributes about one hundred sixty thousand crashes reported to the Department of Safety each year to poor driving habits.

question.text: What does being in shape to drive mean?

answer.text: Being in shape to drive means seeing clearly, being rested, being free of drugs, and being healthy and emotionally fit.

teaching.text: Asked "What does being in shape to drive include?" a tempting wrong answer is "Being able to lift weights", but rested, clear-sighted and drug-free. Remember: Clear, rested, sober, fit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Being in shape to drive means seeing clearly, being rested, being free of drugs, and being healthy and emotionally fit.

question.text: Which temporary conditions can make you unsafe?

answer.text: Temporary conditions such as anger, worry, frustration, fatigue or even a cold can make you an unsafe driver.

teaching.text: Asked "Which temporary condition can make you an unsafe driver?" a tempting wrong answer is "A clean car", but conditions such as a cold. Remember: Moods and colds matter.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Temporary conditions such as anger, worry, frustration, fatigue or even a cold can make you an unsafe driver.

question.text: What should you do if you feel unwell?

answer.text: If you feel unwell, even from a stiff neck, cough or sore leg, let someone else drive.

teaching.text: Asked "You have a stiff neck and a sore leg. What should you do about driving?" a tempting wrong answer is "Drive faster to get home", but let someone else drive. Remember: Let someone else drive.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you feel unwell, even from a stiff neck, cough or sore leg, let someone else drive.

question.text: When may a person with epilepsy drive in Tennessee?

answer.text: In Tennessee, a person with epilepsy may drive if under a doctor's care and seizure-free for at least six months.

teaching.text: The epilepsy and driving rule lets a person with epilepsy drive after six seizure-free months, while the insulin reactions rule keeps an insulin user off the road when a reaction is possible. Remember: Six months seizure-free.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In Tennessee, a person with epilepsy may drive if under a doctor's care and seizure-free for at least six months.

question.text: When should a diabetic on insulin stay off the road?

answer.text: A diabetic on insulin should stay off the road whenever an insulin reaction, blackout, convulsion or shock is possible, for example after skipping a meal.

teaching.text: The epilepsy and driving rule lets a person with epilepsy drive after six seizure-free months, while the insulin reactions rule keeps an insulin user off the road when a reaction is possible. Remember: Reaction risk, stay off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A diabetic on insulin should stay off the road whenever an insulin reaction, blackout, convulsion or shock is possible, for example after skipping a meal.

question.text: Who with heart problems should not drive?

answer.text: People with heart disease, high blood pressure or circulation problems who risk blackouts, fainting or a heart attack should not drive, and anyone treated for a heart condition should ask a doctor about driving.

teaching.text: Asked "Who should ask a doctor about driving?" a tempting wrong answer is "Anyone with a sunburn", but anyone treated for a heart condition. Remember: Blackout risk, no driving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: People with heart disease, high blood pressure or circulation problems who risk blackouts, fainting or a heart attack should not drive, and anyone treated for a heart condition should ask a doctor about driving.

question.text: What should you do if you are angry or impatient before driving?

answer.text: If you are angry or excited, give yourself time to calm down before driving, and if you are impatient, plan extra time for trips so delays do not tempt you to speed.

teaching.text: Asked "You are impatient about being late. What should you do?" a tempting wrong answer is "Speed to make up time", but plan extra time. Remember: Calm down, allow time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you are angry or excited, give yourself time to calm down before driving, and if you are impatient, plan extra time for trips so delays do not tempt you to speed.

question.text: Can a skilled driver drive safely when buzzed?

answer.text: No one, regardless of skill or experience, can drive safely when buzzed or impaired by alcohol or drugs.

teaching.text: Asked "Can a very skilled driver drive safely when buzzed?" a tempting wrong answer is "Yes, with experience", but no one can. Remember: Buzzed is impaired.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No one, regardless of skill or experience, can drive safely when buzzed or impaired by alcohol or drugs.

question.text: How does night affect everyone's vision?

answer.text: Everyone sees worse at night, and some drivers struggle with the glare of oncoming headlights.

teaching.text: Asked "How does night affect drivers' vision?" a tempting wrong answer is "Only older drivers see worse", but everyone sees worse. Remember: Night dims everyone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Everyone sees worse at night, and some drivers struggle with the glare of oncoming headlights.

question.text: What should you do if you struggle to see at night?

answer.text: If you have trouble seeing at night, limit night driving to what is necessary and be very careful when you do.

teaching.text: Asked "You have trouble seeing at night. What should you do?" a tempting wrong answer is "Drive faster at night", but limit night driving. Remember: Limit night driving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you have trouble seeing at night, limit night driving to what is necessary and be very careful when you do.

question.text: When does judging distance and speed matter most?

answer.text: Judging distance and speed takes practice and matters most when merging and when judging gaps to pass on two-lane roads.

teaching.text: Asked "When does judging distance and speed matter most?" a tempting wrong answer is "When parked", but when merging and passing. Remember: Merging and passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Judging distance and speed takes practice and matters most when merging and when judging gaps to pass on two-lane roads.

question.text: How often should an eye specialist check your eyes?

answer.text: Because seeing well is so important, have your eyes checked by an eye specialist every year or two.

teaching.text: Asked "How often should an eye specialist check your eyes?" a tempting wrong answer is "Every ten years", but every year or two. Remember: Eyes checked yearly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Because seeing well is so important, have your eyes checked by an eye specialist every year or two.

question.text: What does the corrective lens restriction require?

answer.text: If your license shows the corrective lens restriction, code one, you must wear your glasses or contacts at all times while driving, or you could be ticketed and fined.

teaching.text: The corrective lens restriction rule makes lenses mandatory under the code one restriction, and the always wear your lenses rule says to wear them even on short trips and keep a spare. Remember: Lenses on, always.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your license shows the corrective lens restriction, code one, you must wear your glasses or contacts at all times while driving, or you could be ticketed and fined.

question.text: Should you wear your glasses even on short trips?

answer.text: If you need glasses or contacts, wear them even on short trips, and keep a spare pair in the vehicle.

teaching.text: The corrective lens restriction rule makes lenses mandatory under the code one restriction, and the always wear your lenses rule says to wear them even on short trips and keep a spare. Remember: Short trips too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you need glasses or contacts, wear them even on short trips, and keep a spare pair in the vehicle.

question.text: Should you wear dark sunglasses at night?

answer.text: Do not wear dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night, since they cut the light you need to see.

teaching.text: Asked "Why should you not wear dark sunglasses at night?" a tempting wrong answer is "They are fine at night", but they cut the light you need. Remember: No dark lenses at night.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not wear dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night, since they cut the light you need to see.

question.text: How does hearing help a driver?

answer.text: Hearing helps you notice horns, sirens and screeching tires, and hearing-impaired drivers can compensate with their vision.

teaching.text: Asked "How can hearing-impaired drivers compensate?" a tempting wrong answer is "By driving faster", but with their vision. Remember: Hear horns and sirens.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hearing helps you notice horns, sirens and screeching tires, and hearing-impaired drivers can compensate with their vision.

question.text: How can you avoid fatigue before a long trip?

answer.text: To avoid fatigue, get a normal night's sleep, eat lightly before a long trip, avoid medicine that causes drowsiness, and try not to drive when you would normally be asleep.

teaching.text: The preventing fatigue rule lists steps to prevent fatigue before a trip, while the hourly breaks rule says to stop for a break every hour on long drives. Remember: Sleep, eat light.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To avoid fatigue, get a normal night's sleep, eat lightly before a long trip, avoid medicine that causes drowsiness, and try not to drive when you would normally be asleep.

question.text: How often should you stop on long drives?

answer.text: On long drives, stop for a break every hour or more often if needed, walking around and getting fresh air and a drink.

teaching.text: The preventing fatigue rule lists steps to prevent fatigue before a trip, while the hourly breaks rule says to stop for a break every hour on long drives. Remember: Break every hour.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On long drives, stop for a break every hour or more often if needed, walking around and getting fresh air and a drink.

question.text: What should you do if you feel sleepy while driving?

answer.text: Never drive while sleepy; pulling over for a few hours of sleep beats gambling that you can stay awake.

teaching.text: Asked "You feel sleepy behind the wheel. What does the manual advise?" a tempting wrong answer is "Turn up the radio and push on", but pull over to sleep. Remember: Pull over and sleep.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never drive while sleepy; pulling over for a few hours of sleep beats gambling that you can stay awake.

question.text: Which signs mean a mechanic should check your brakes?

answer.text: Have a mechanic check your brakes if they seem weak, are noisy, smell odd or the pedal sinks to the floor.

teaching.text: Asked "Your brake pedal sinks to the floor. What should you do?" a tempting wrong answer is "Pump harder and keep driving", but have a mechanic check them. Remember: Weak, noisy, sinking.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Have a mechanic check your brakes if they seem weak, are noisy, smell odd or the pedal sinks to the floor.

question.text: How should you check your lights?

answer.text: Check turn signals, brake lights, taillights and headlights from outside the vehicle.

teaching.text: Asked "How should you check your turn signals, brake lights and headlights?" a tempting wrong answer is "Only from the driver's seat", but from outside the vehicle. Remember: Check from outside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Check turn signals, brake lights, taillights and headlights from outside the vehicle.

question.text: When do batteries run down faster?

answer.text: Batteries run down faster in cold or damp weather, and keeping jumper cables in the car can get you started again.

teaching.text: Asked "Why keep jumper cables in the car?" a tempting wrong answer is "To tow other cars", but to restart a run-down battery. Remember: Cold drains batteries.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Batteries run down faster in cold or damp weather, and keeping jumper cables in the car can get you started again.

question.text: Why fix a cracked windshield?

answer.text: Repair or replace a damaged windshield, since cracked glass can break in a minor collision, and replace wiper blades that no longer clear the glass.

teaching.text: Asked "Why repair a cracked windshield?" a tempting wrong answer is "For looks only", but cracked glass can break. Remember: Cracked glass breaks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Repair or replace a damaged windshield, since cracked glass can break in a minor collision, and replace wiper blades that no longer clear the glass.

question.text: When should you check washer fluid?

answer.text: Check the non-freezing washer fluid level each time you fill up with gas, and clean the windshield at gas stops so sun or headlights do not blur your view.

teaching.text: Asked "When should you check the washer fluid level?" a tempting wrong answer is "Once every five years", but each fill-up. Remember: Check at each fill-up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Check the non-freezing washer fluid level each time you fill up with gas, and clean the windshield at gas stops so sun or headlights do not blur your view.

question.text: What can worn or bald tires do?

answer.text: Worn or bald tires lengthen stopping distance, make turning harder on wet roads, raise the chance of a flat and can cause hydroplaning.

teaching.text: The worn tires rule lists the dangers of worn tires, while the penny test rule explains the penny test for when tread is too shallow. Remember: Bald tires slide.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Worn or bald tires lengthen stopping distance, make turning harder on wet roads, raise the chance of a flat and can cause hydroplaning.

question.text: How does the penny test work?

answer.text: In the penny test, insert a penny head first into the tread; if the tread does not reach Lincoln's head, two thirty-seconds inch, the tire is illegal and unsafe and must be replaced.

teaching.text: The worn tires rule lists the dangers of worn tires, while the penny test rule explains the penny test for when tread is too shallow. Remember: Lincoln's head shows: replace.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In the penny test, insert a penny head first into the tread; if the tread does not reach Lincoln's head, two thirty-seconds inch, the tire is illegal and unsafe and must be replaced.

question.text: What do unbalanced tires and low pressure cause?

answer.text: Unbalanced tires and low pressure wear tires faster, waste fuel and make the vehicle harder to steer and stop.

teaching.text: Asked "What do unbalanced tires and low pressure cause?" a tempting wrong answer is "Better handling", but harder steering and stopping. Remember: Wear, waste, worse handling.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unbalanced tires and low pressure wear tires faster, waste fuel and make the vehicle harder to steer and stop.

question.text: Which tire pressure should you use?

answer.text: Use the recommended tire pressure on the sticker in the driver's door jamb, not the pressure printed on the tire, which is only the tire's maximum.

teaching.text: The door jamb tire pressure rule says to use the door jamb pressure, while the aftermarket tire pressure rule says that figure no longer applies to aftermarket tires of a different size. Remember: Door jamb, not tire.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use the recommended tire pressure on the sticker in the driver's door jamb, not the pressure printed on the tire, which is only the tire's maximum.

question.text: What pressure should you use for aftermarket tires of a different size?

answer.text: If you have put on aftermarket tires of a different size, ask the tire maker or installer for the right pressure, since the door-jamb figure no longer applies.

teaching.text: The door jamb tire pressure rule says to use the door jamb pressure, while the aftermarket tire pressure rule says that figure no longer applies to aftermarket tires of a different size. Remember: Ask the tire maker.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you have put on aftermarket tires of a different size, ask the tire maker or installer for the right pressure, since the door-jamb figure no longer applies.

question.text: What signs mean the shocks need checking?

answer.text: If the car keeps bouncing after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, have a mechanic check the shocks and suspension.

teaching.text: Asked "Your car keeps bouncing after a bump. What should you have checked?" a tempting wrong answer is "The radio", but the shocks and suspension. Remember: Bouncing means shocks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the car keeps bouncing after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, have a mechanic check the shocks and suspension.

question.text: Why never turn the ignition to lock while moving?

answer.text: Never turn the ignition to the lock position while the car is moving, because the steering wheel will lock and you will lose control.

teaching.text: The never lock the ignition moving rule warns that locking the ignition while moving locks the steering, while the do not freeze or jerk rule warns against jerking the wheel. Remember: Ignition lock locks steering.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never turn the ignition to the lock position while the car is moving, because the steering wheel will lock and you will lose control.

question.text: What can a sleepy feeling while driving signal?

answer.text: A sleepy feeling while driving or riding may mean an exhaust leak, which must be fixed at once because exhaust gases can kill inside a vehicle in a very short time.

teaching.text: The exhaust leak warning rule says a sleepy feeling may mean an exhaust leak, while the blocked tailpipe danger rule says never run the engine where the tailpipe may be blocked. Remember: Sleepy may mean exhaust.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A sleepy feeling while driving or riding may mean an exhaust leak, which must be fixed at once because exhaust gases can kill inside a vehicle in a very short time.

question.text: Where must you never run the engine?

answer.text: Never run the engine in a closed garage or wherever the tailpipe may be blocked, including when the car is stuck in mud or snow.

teaching.text: The exhaust leak warning rule says a sleepy feeling may mean an exhaust leak, while the blocked tailpipe danger rule says never run the engine where the tailpipe may be blocked. Remember: Never with blocked exhaust.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never run the engine in a closed garage or wherever the tailpipe may be blocked, including when the car is stuck in mud or snow.

question.text: What should you do when idling for a long time?

answer.text: When idling for a long time, open a window for fresh air, and never sleep or sit with the engine running during an extended rest stop.

teaching.text: The blocked tailpipe danger rule forbids running the engine with the tailpipe blocked, while the fresh air while idling rule says to open a window when idling and never sleep with the engine running. Remember: Window open, never sleep.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When idling for a long time, open a window for fresh air, and never sleep or sit with the engine running during an extended rest stop.

question.text: When should you check the radiator?

answer.text: Check the radiator only when the engine is cool, and keep coolant at the level the owner's manual recommends to prevent overheating or freezing.

teaching.text: Asked "When should you check the radiator?" a tempting wrong answer is "Right after a long drive", but only when cool. Remember: Only when cool.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Check the radiator only when the engine is cool, and keep coolant at the level the owner's manual recommends to prevent overheating or freezing.

question.text: How much gas should you have before a long trip?

answer.text: Make sure your vehicle has at least a half tank of gas before any trip of significant length.

teaching.text: Asked "Before a trip of significant length, how much gas should you have?" a tempting wrong answer is "Just enough to start", but at least a half tank. Remember: Half a tank.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Make sure your vehicle has at least a half tank of gas before any trip of significant length.

question.text: Why keep loose objects off the floor?

answer.text: Keep loose objects off the floor where they could roll under the brake pedal, and secure items that could hit someone in a sudden stop.

teaching.text: Asked "Why keep loose objects off the floor?" a tempting wrong answer is "They scratch the floor", but they could roll under the pedal. Remember: Nothing under the pedal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep loose objects off the floor where they could roll under the brake pedal, and secure items that could hit someone in a sudden stop.

question.text: What is the horn for?

answer.text: Use the horn only as a warning to others.

teaching.text: Asked "What should you use the horn for?" a tempting wrong answer is "To greet friends", but only as a warning. Remember: Horn warns only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use the horn only as a warning to others.

question.text: How big a cushion should you keep behind the car ahead?

answer.text: Keep at least a two-second cushion behind the vehicle ahead, and more when conditions are hazardous.

teaching.text: Asked "How much cushion should you keep behind the vehicle ahead?" a tempting wrong answer is "Half a second", but at least two seconds. Remember: Two seconds or more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep at least a two-second cushion behind the vehicle ahead, and more when conditions are hazardous.

question.text: Why do multi-vehicle crashes happen in traffic flow?

answer.text: Vehicles moving the same direction at the same speed cannot hit one another, and multi-vehicle crashes often happen when drivers go faster or slower than traffic.

teaching.text: The moving with traffic rule says vehicles at the same speed cannot hit one another, while the slow where people gather rule says to slow down where people and traffic gather. Remember: Match traffic speed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles moving the same direction at the same speed cannot hit one another, and multi-vehicle crashes often happen when drivers go faster or slower than traffic.

question.text: Where should you slow down for crowds and traffic?

answer.text: Slow down where people and traffic gather, such as when brake lights come on several cars ahead, in shopping centers and downtown areas, and at rush hour.

teaching.text: The moving with traffic rule says vehicles at the same speed cannot hit one another, while the slow where people gather rule says to slow down where people and traffic gather. Remember: Slow where people gather.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Slow down where people and traffic gather, such as when brake lights come on several cars ahead, in shopping centers and downtown areas, and at rush hour.

question.text: Why adjust speed on narrow bridges and in tunnels?

answer.text: On narrow bridges and in tunnels, approaching vehicles pass closer together, so adjust your speed.

teaching.text: The narrow bridges and tunnels rule says to adjust speed on narrow bridges and in tunnels, while the railroad crossings rule says to make sure no train is coming and you have room to cross. Remember: Closer passing, slower.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On narrow bridges and in tunnels, approaching vehicles pass closer together, so adjust your speed.

question.text: What should you watch for near schools and playgrounds?

answer.text: Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, always watch for children who may cross, run or ride into the street without looking.

teaching.text: Asked "Near schools and playgrounds, what should you always watch for?" a tempting wrong answer is "Only school buses", but children running into the street. Remember: Children dart out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, always watch for children who may cross, run or ride into the street without looking.

question.text: What must you check at railroad crossings?

answer.text: At railroad crossings, make sure no train is coming and you have room to get across, and slow down on bumpy crossings.

teaching.text: The narrow bridges and tunnels rule says to adjust speed on narrow bridges and in tunnels, while the railroad crossings rule says to make sure no train is coming and you have room to cross. Remember: No train, room across.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At railroad crossings, make sure no train is coming and you have room to get across, and slow down on bumpy crossings.

question.text: What should good drivers do after moving to a new state?

answer.text: Good drivers review the manual periodically for law changes and study the driver manual of any new state they move to, even when no test is required.

teaching.text: Asked "You move to a new state where no test is required. What should a good driver do?" a tempting wrong answer is "Nothing", but study the new state's manual. Remember: Study the new manual.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Good drivers review the manual periodically for law changes and study the driver manual of any new state they move to, even when no test is required.
